text: Charles Kao argued in 1966 that fibre's 1,000 dB/km attenuation was not a property of glass. What was it?
choices: Impurities — principally iron, copper and hydroxyl contamination
Bending losses in the test apparatus
explanation: Kao argued pure silica should manage 20 dB/km, and spent years persuading glass manufacturers to make purer glass. Corning succeeded in 1970; modern single-mode fibre achieves about 0.17 dB/km at 1550 nm. He received the Nobel Prize in 2009.
